questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with relapsed CLL is being considered for a clinical trial involving an investigational drug targeting MCL-1, a protein involved in the regulation of apoptosis. Which of the following best describes the role of MCL-1 in cell survival and apoptosis?

options.label: A
options.text: MCL-1 promotes apoptosis by binding to pro-apoptotic proteins such as BAX and BAK.

options.label: B
options.text: MCL-1 is a BCL-2 family member that prevents apoptosis

options.label: C
options.text: MCL-1 directly activates caspases, which leads to cell apoptosis.

options.label: D
options.text: MCL-1 enhances apoptosis by inhibiting the release of cytochrome c from mitochondria.

questions.answerText: MCL-1 is a BCL-2 family member that prevents apoptosis
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) MCL-1 is a BCL-2 family member that prevents apoptosis

questions.stem: A 10-year-old girl presented to her pediatrician with a 5-week history of painful, swollen joints and recent onset dyspnea. Physical exam revealed a temperature of 390° C, cervical lymphadenopathy and pansystolic and diastolic murmurs. Laboratory analysis was positive for serum antibodies to streptolysin O. Although she was admitted to the hospital, she died of progressive heart failure. Which of the following is the proposed pathogenesis of this disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Antibodies to streptococcus cross-react with heart antigens

options.label: B
options.text: Bioactive products released by the tumor cause fibrosis

options.label: C
options.text: Direct toxicity of catecholamines on cardiac myocytes

options.label: D
options.text: Endocardial trauma acts as a nidus for sterile vegetations

questions.answerText: Antibodies to streptococcus cross-react with heart antigens
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Antibodies to streptococcus cross-react with heart antigens

questions.stemHtml: A 25-year-old Caucasian boy presented with several months of abdominal pain, fever and dark colored urine. Hams test was positive and flow cytometry graph was done to confirm the diagnosis. Which is incorrect about this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Normal cells have only one active PIGA gene Increased LDH and decreased levels of haptoglobin

options.label: D
options.text: BMT is the treatment of choice

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Thrombocytopenia is very common 

 

Abdominal pain due to venous thrombosis….dark colored urine… hemoglobinuria 

 

Increased risk of Aplastic anemia (AA) and Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)…..thrombocytopenia is rare. 

 

Pegcetacoplan is a pegylated peptide targeting complement protein C3. Eculizumab and ravulizumab also used. BMT is definitive treatment of choice.

questions.stem: A 51-year-old woman with a significant family history of early-onset breast and ovarian cancer undergoes genetic screening. The results reveal a pathogenic variant in the BRCA1 gene. Which of the following best describes the primary role of the BRCA1 gene in cellular function?

options.label: D
options.text: Encodes a cell surface receptor for growth factors

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Repairs double-strand DNA breaks

questions.stemHtml: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis controlled on therapy for last 6 months came to you with the complaints of fatigue, headache shortness of breath and diarrhea after meals. His peripheral smear is shown. Which of the following is true about this patient?

options.label: D
options.text: BM shows cells with nuclear cytoplasmic

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) RBC folate levels are reduced

questions.stemHtml: A 15-year-old female presents with recurrent abdominal pain and melena. Physical examination reveals multiple pigmented macules on her lips, buccal mucosa, and fingers. An upper endoscopy reveals multiple hamartomatous polyps in the small intestine which have STK11 gene mutation on genetic analsis. Which of the following complications is she at greatest risk for?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Intussusception

 

Polyps, Pigmentation, Positive family history help in diagnosis as STK11 mutations may be missing in some patients.  PJ Disease: Pigmentation, Jejunal polyps Dominant 

 

  • One of the most common and immediate complications in patients with PJS is Intussusception due to the large size and numerous polyps, leading to bowel obstruction.
  • Melanotic pigmentation can be seen in Addison disease, hemochromatosis, fibrous dysplasia of bone (Albright syndrome).

questions.stemHtml: A 55-year-old male presented with fatigue, infection and left sided abdominal pain. On his workup, on a bone marrow sample that contained a B cell clonal population having TRAP and annexin A1 positivity. All of the following are true for this patient except:

options.label: A
options.text: Smear shows pancytopenia with cells having a characteristic serrated cytoplasmic border

options.label: B
options.text: Molecular testing shall detect BRAF V600E mutation

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Lymph node involvement is common

 

  • LN involvement is rare. Vemurafenib is used.
  • Rare cases that are BRAF V600E mutation negative will be positive for IGHV4-34
  • Lymphadenopathy is rare in classical HCL.
  • Instead, HCL cells prefer spleen and bone marrow, especially the red pulp of the spleen.
  • If lymph nodes are involved, it's atypical or seen in HCL-variant, not classical HCL.

 

Clinical Scenario Analysis:

 

  • 55-year-old man with:
    • Fatigue, infection, and left-sided abdominal pain
    • Suggestive of cytopenia + splenomegaly
  • Bone marrow: B-cell clonal population with:
    • TRAP positivity (tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase)
    • Annexin A1 positivity
    • These features are highly specific for  Hairy Cell Leukemia (HCL)
    • Hairy Cell Leukemia (HCL) is a rare B-cell chronic lymphoproliferative disorder.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Smear shows pancytopenia with cells having a characteristic serrated cytoplasmic border: True. Classic description.

 

  • The leukemic cells have "hairy" projections (cytoplasmic projections), giving the cells a serrated ("hairy") appearance.
  • Peripheral blood often shows pancytopenia (especially monocytopenia).

 

Option B. Molecular testing shall detect BRAF V600E mutation: True. 

 

  • >90% of HCL patients harbor the BRAF V600E mutation.
  • This is a driver mutation and helps distinguish HCL from other B-cell neoplasms like HCL-variant and splenic marginal zone lymphoma.

 

Option D. Excellent prognosis: True.

 

  • HCL has an excellent response to purine analogs like cladribine or pentostatin
  • Long-term remissions are common, with survival often extending over 10–15 years or more.

 

Key Points About Hairy Cell Leukemia (HCL):

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy of Mediterranean descent presents with pallor, fatigue, and hepatosplenomegaly. Complete blood count shows severe microcytic, hypochromic anemia with a hemoglobin level of 6.5 g/dL. Hemoglobin electrophoresis reveals an increase in HbF and HbA2. Which of the following is the most likely genetic mutation responsible for this patient’s condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Mutation in the gene encoding spectrin

options.label: C
options.text: Point mutation in the promoter region of the β-globin gene

options.label: D
options.text: Frameshift mutation leading to a truncated γ-globin chain

questions.answerText: Point mutation in the promoter region of the β-globin gene
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Point mutation in the promoter region of the β-globin gene

 

This patient likely has β-thalassemia major, characterized by severe anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, and increased HbF and HbA2. The most common mutations in β-thalassemia are point mutations in the promoter or coding region of the β-globin gene, which reduce or eliminate β-globin synthesis, causing an imbalance in α- and β-globin production.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with fatigue, night sweats, and splenomegaly. His white blood cell count is 120,000/µL with a differential showing a high number of immature granulocytes. Molecular studies reveal the presence of the BCR-ABL fusion gene. Which of the following is the primary function of the BCR-ABL fusion protein in CML?

options.label: A
options.text: It prevents apoptosis by upregulating BCL-2

options.label: B
options.text: It functions as a constitutively active tyrosine kinase

options.label: C
options.text: It inhibits cellular senescence by activating telomerase

options.label: D
options.text: It increases erythropoietin sensitivity in hematopoietic cells

questions.answerText: It functions as a constitutively active tyrosine kinase
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) It functions as a constitutively active tyrosine kinase

 

The BCR-ABL fusion protein, resulting from the t(9;22) translocation (Philadelphia chromosome), acts as a constitutively active tyrosine kinase. This continuous signaling drives uncontrolled proliferation of myeloid cells, a hallmark of CML. Targeted therapy with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., imatinib) directly inhibits BCR-ABL.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old lady woman presents with endometrial carcinoma. Her mother died of endometrial cancer at age 50, and her 42-year-old brother was recently diagnosed with colon cancer. You suspect a familial cancer syndrome. Which gene in this family is most likely to be mutated?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) MSH 2

 

  • The familial pattern of cancers (endometrial carcinoma & colon cancer) suggests Lynch syndrome/HNPCC: AD condition; mutations in mismatch repair (MMR) genes.
  • The one most likely to be mutated in Lynch syndrome is MSH2. Lynch syndrome commonly involves mutations in MMR genes such as MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, and PMS2.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with a palpable lump in her left breast with bloody nipple discharge. A core needle biopsy is performed, and histopathology reveals sheets of small, pleomorphic cells infiltrating the stroma with the formation of glandular structures. Which of the following is not true for her?

options.label: A
options.text: Diamino benzidine is used for brown color in IHC.

options.label: B
options.text: For a score 2 in IHC, Fluorescence in situ hybridization is indicated.

options.label: C
options.text: Under activity of CDH1 gene tends to be bilateral and multifocal.

options.label: D
options.text: Over expression of E cadherin has association with familial gastric cancer.

questions.answerText: Over expression of E cadherin has association with familial gastric cancer.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Over expression of E cadherin has association with familial gastric cancer.

 

Under activity of E cadherin has association with familial gastric cancer.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child of Sindh area of Gujarat descent presents with mild fatigue and pallor. Laboratory results show a hemoglobin of 10.2 g/dL, MCV of 68 fL, and an RBC count of 5.8 million cells/µL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) β-thalassemia minor

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with bone pain, anemia, and recurrent infections. Laboratory tests reveal a serum creatinine of 2.1 mg/dL and hypercalcemia. Serum protein electrophoresis shows an M-spike, and urine protein electrophoresis is positive for Bence-Jones proteins. Which of the following findings would be most indicative of the underlying pathophysiology in this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Increased production of immunoglobulin G polyclonal antibodies

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Elevated serum levels of β2-microglobulin

 

MM has monoclonal proliferation of plasma cells, which produce a single type of immunoglobulin, leading to the M-spike seen on electrophoresis. β2-microglobulin levels correlate with tumor burden and are often elevated in multiple myeloma, serving as a prognostic marker.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) 1 and 2

 

SCA has High MF..low OF…IDA has reduced HbA2..DL antibody is cold hemolysin disease

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with chronic kidney disease receives a blood transfusion. Thirty minutes into the transfusion, he develops chills, a fever of 38.9°C (102°F), and mild hypotension. The transfusion is stopped, and there are no signs of hemolysis. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of his reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Alloantibodies directed against donor red blood cell antigens

options.label: B
options.text: Release of cytokines from donor leukocytes during storage

options.label: C
options.text: IgG antibodies that recognize IgA in the infused blood product

options.label: D
options.text: Activation of HLA antibodies on the neutrophils of recipient

questions.answerText: Release of cytokines from donor leukocytes during storage
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans B) Release of cytokines from donor leukocytes during storage

 

FNHTR is due to release of cytokines from donor leukocytes during storage (Leukoreduction before storage can reduce this risk.)

 

Option d…TRALI…..option C ..anaphylaxis in IgA deficiency

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Irradiation of blood products

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Sirtuins act by deacetylating specific transcription factors

options.label: C
options.text: Have 7 subtype and reduce insulin sensitivity

options.label: D
options.text: Sirtuins induce apoptosis to remove damaged cells and prevent tumorigenesis

questions.answerText: Have 7 subtype and reduce insulin sensitivity
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Have 7 subtype and reduce insulin sensitivity

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true about Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH)?

options.label: A
options.text: Use of probes with fluorescent dyes applied to metaphase spreads or interphase nuclei.

options.label: B
options.text: Analysis can be performed on cells from chorionic villus biopsy or umbilical cord blood

options.label: C
options.text: Mandatory requirement of rapidly dividing cells

options.label: D
options.text: Detection of aneuploidy, subtle microdeletions and complex translocations

questions.answerText: Mandatory requirement of rapidly dividing cells
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Mandatory requirement of rapidly dividing cells

 

FISH to circumvent the need for dividing cells is invaluable when a rapid diagnosis is needed (e.g., in a critically ill infant suspected of having an underlying genetic disorder). 

 

FISH is for detection of numeric abnormalities of chromosomes (aneuploidy), subtle microdeletions and complex translocations not indentifiable by routine karyotyping, and gene amplification (e.g., MYCN amplification in neuroblastomas).

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man in India requires an urgent blood transfusion. He is tested as blood type "O" but experiences an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction after receiving "O" type blood. Which of the following best explains the cause of his transfusion reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Anti-A and anti-B antibodies that react with minor antigens in "O" blood

options.label: B
options.text: Presence of anti-H antibodies that react with the H antigen in standard "O" blood

options.label: C
options.text: Isohemagglutinins directed against unknown antigens due to the hh phenotype

options.label: D
options.text: Mutation in Rh antigen that causes auto-antibody production after transfusion

questions.answerText: Presence of anti-H antibodies that react with the H antigen in standard "O" blood
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Presence of anti-H antibodies that react with the H antigen in standard "O" blood

 

Further testing reveals he has the Bombay blood group (hh phenotype).

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old man presented to his general practitioner with a two-week history of right-sided flank pain. Urinalysis showed hematuria. A CT guided biopsy was done having the image. Which of the following risk factors is most closely linked to the development of this disease?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Tobacco abuse

questions.stem: A 25-year-old female presents to the emergency department with fever, hypotension, diffuse erythematous rash, and confusion. She reports recent use of tampons during menstruation. Laboratory studies reveal leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and elevated liver enzymes. Blood and urine cultures are obtained, and she is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics and intravenous fluids. Which of the following is true about the antigen involved here?

options.label: A
options.text: Binds to B7 and CD28 co-stimulatory molecules

options.label: B
options.text: Binds to the beta chain of TCR and MHC class II molecules of APC stimulating T cell activation

options.label: C
options.text: Binds to the CD4 + molecule causing T cell activation

options.label: D
options.text: Is presented by macrophages to a larger-than-normal number of T helper CD4 + lymphocytes

questions.answerText: Binds to the beta chain of TCR and MHC class II molecules of APC stimulating T cell activation
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Binds to the beta chain of TCR and MHC class II molecules of APC stimulating T cell activation

 

Super-antigens bridge the TCR on T cells and MHC class II on antigen-presenting cells outside the conventional peptide-binding groove, leading to widespread T cell activation without the need for specific antigen recognition.

questions.stem: A postnatal day 12 male infant presented with thrombocytopenia. Cardiopulmonary and abdomen examination showed no obvious abnormalities. Results of blood tests before admission had leucocytosis and thrombocytopenia. The family history documented that the disease had autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?

options.label: B
options.text: Deficiency of Wiskott Aldrich syndrome protein

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Deficiency of WIP protein

 

Deficiency of WAS protein interacting protein (WIP deficiency) is AR,

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with prolonged bleeding following a recent tooth extraction. She denies any recent trauma or family history of bleeding disorders. Laboratory tests reveal a prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) of 68 seconds (normal range: 25-35 seconds) that does not correct upon mixing with normal plasma. Prothrombin time (PT) and platelet count are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Acquired hemophilia

 

Acquired hemophilia is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the development of antibodies (inhibitors) against clotting factors, commonly factor VIII, which leads to an isolated prolonged aPTT that does not correct with mixing studies. This condition is typically seen in older adults or those with underlying autoimmune diseases or malignancies

 

A prolonged aPTT with normal PT and platelet count indicates a problem in the intrinsic pathway (factors VIII, IX, XI, XII). 

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Von Willebrand disease:

 

  • Often causes mucosal bleeding.
  • Can prolong aPTT mildly due to decreased factor VIII (vWF carries factor VIII).
  • However, mixing studies correct the aPTT, because it’s a factor deficiency, not an inhibitor.

 

Option B. Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency):

 

  • X-linked; usually seen in males.
  • Presents early in life, not suddenly at age 52.
  • Mixing study corrects aPTT in inherited hemophilia.
  • Unlikely in a woman with no prior history.

 

Option D. Lupus anticoagulant:

 

  • Actually a prothrombotic condition, despite the name.
  • Causes prolonged aPTT, but not associated with bleeding.
  • aPTT does not correct on mixing — true — but again, no bleeding tendency.
  • Doesn’t fit the bleeding history

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a painless neck mass. Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of the nodule reveals papillary thyroid carcinoma with nuclear grooves and intranuclear inclusions. A total thyroidectomy is performed, and pathology confirms a 2.5 cm tumor without extrathyroidal extension. Further genetic analysis reveals a BRAF V600E mutation in the tumor cells. Which of the following is true about this cancer?

options.label: B
options.text: Better response to radioactive iodine therapy

options.label: D
options.text: Increased risk of aggressive histologic variants

questions.answerText: Increased risk of aggressive histologic variants
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Increased risk of aggressive histologic variants

 

The BRAF V600E mutation in papillary thyroid carcinoma is associated with more aggressive disease, including an increased risk of certain histologic variants, such as the tall cell variant, which are more likely to exhibit aggressive behavior. Patients with BRAF-mutated tumors often have higher recurrence rates and may show poorer responses to radioactive iodine therapy.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man presents with a history of recent behavioral changes, tremors, and abdominal pain. Physical examination reveals hepatomegaly and mild ataxia. Laboratory tests show elevated liver enzymes and low serum ceruloplasmin. Which of the following histologic findings is most characteristic of the liver pathology seen in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Rhodanine-positive granules


Rhodanine staining: highlights copper deposits (appearing as orange-red granules within hepatocytes, which is characteristic of Wilson disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not correctly matched?

options.label: C
options.text: Saline washed red cells: reduced risk of allergic reactions

options.label: D
options.text: Cryo poor plasma: contraindicated in HUS/TTP

questions.answerText: Cryo poor plasma: contraindicated in HUS/TTP
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Cryo poor plasma: contraindicated in HUS/TTP   

 

Cryo poor plasma is cryosupernatant is plasma from which cryoprecipitate is removed. It is useful for the treatment of TTP or treatment of HUS by plasma exchange.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about the condition having cells as shown with an inflammatory background? The cells are of B cell origin and have CD30 + and PAX 5 +Commonest site affected is the Waldeyer ring Nodular sclerosis variant commonly involves the mediastinum Lymphocyte predominant variant has poor prognosis Eosinophilia is rare in mixed cellularity variant
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Only 2, 4 and 5

 

2. Commonest site affected is the Waldeyer ring: Incorrect.

 

  • Waldeyer’s ring involvement is uncommon in Hodgkin lymphoma.
  • It is more characteristic of Non-Hodgkin lymphomas, especially diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).
  • Hodgkin lymphoma commonly affects cervical, mediastinal, and axillary lymph nodes.
  • So this is a wrong statement.

 

4. Lymphocyte predominant variant has poor prognosis: Incorrect.

 

  • Nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) has a good prognosis.
  • It shows:
    • CD20+, CD45+
    • CD15–, CD30–
    • Popcorn cells instead of classic RS cells
  • So this statement is wrong.

 

5. Eosinophilia is rare in mixed cellularity variant: Incorrect.

 

  • Mixed cellularity variant commonly shows eosinophils in the background.
  • This subtype has a rich inflammatory infiltrate including eosinophils, plasma cells, and histiocytes.
  • Seen more in HIV-positive patients and developing countries.
  • So this is also incorrect.

 

Other Statements:

 

1. The cells are of B cell origin and have CD30+ and PAX5+: True.

  • Reed-Sternberg (RS) cells in classical Hodgkin lymphoma are:
  • CD30 positive
  • PAX5 weakly positive (indicating B-cell lineage)
  • Usually CD15+, CD20−
  • So this is a correct statement.

 

3. Nodular sclerosis variant commonly involves the mediastinum: True.

  • Nodular sclerosis is the most common subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
  • Mediastinal involvement is very common, especially in young women.
  • So this is a correct statement.

 

Incorrect statements are:

 

  • 2 (Waldeyer's ring)
  • 4 (Lymphocyte predominant = good prognosis)
  • 5 (Eosinophilia is common, not rare, in mixed cellularity)

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presents with abdominal pain and a CT reveals a mass within the gastrointestinal system, which is resected. Histopathologic examination reveals a submucosal mass composed of spindle cells with lightly eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in a syncytial pattern. Which of the following options correlates with an unfavorable prognosis for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) High mitotic index

 

GIST findings suggesting a more favorable prognosis include: stomach location, tumor size ≤ 2 cm, mitotic rate < 5 per 50 HPF, R0 (a resection with negative margins) and the presence of a KIT mutation.

 

  • Strongest independent adverse prognostic factor.
  • High mitotic count (e.g., >5 per 50 high-power fields) = high proliferative activity = poor prognosis.
  • Even small GISTs with a high mitotic rate can behave aggressively.
  • This is a key unfavorable prognostic marker.
  • Histopathology:
    • Submucosal mass
    • Spindle cells
    • Lightly eosinophilic cytoplasm
    • Syncytial pattern
    • These are classic features of GIST.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. KIT mutation present:

 

  • Common, but NOT an unfavorable prognostic marker.
  • ~75–80% of GISTs have KIT (CD117) mutations.
  • Some KIT mutations respond well to imatinib, especially exon 11.
  • Not all KIT mutations confer worse prognosis — some are actually predictive of better response to therapy.
  • Not an indicator of poor prognosis.

 

Option B. Mass located in the Stomach

 

  • Gastric GISTs → better prognosis
  • Jejunal/ileal/colonic GISTs → worse outcomes

 

Option D. Mass 10 cm in greatest dimension

 

  • Tumor size >5 cm is associated with worse prognosis.

questions.stem: "Moldy" grains in some low socio economic area populated areas contain a substance that causes a specific G-to-T mutation in gene p53. The population in these regions is expected to be at an increased risk of which of the following diseases?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Liver cancer

 

High levels of dietary aflatoxin exposure is associated with a G-C→ T: A transversion in codon 249 of the p53 gene, a mutation thought to greatly increase the risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma.

questions.stemHtml: A 34-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fatigue, easy bruising, and gum bleeding. Physical examination reveals pallor, petechiae on her lower extremities, and mild hepatosplenomegaly. A bone marrow biopsy is performed and shows numerous blasts with appearance as in image. Which of the following translocations is most commonly associated with this finding?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) t(15;17)

 

Faggot cells have bundle of stick appearance….are highly characteristic of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL).

questions.stem: A 58-year-old male presents with vague abdominal discomfort and early satiety. A CT scan of the abdomen reveals a 6 cm mass in the stomach. Endoscopic biopsy shows spindle-shaped cells with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD117 and DOG1. Which of the following is not a marker for gastrointestinal stromal tumor?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) NRG-1

 

GIST can be associated with KIT, PDGFR and SDH mutation the latter being involved in Carney Stratakis syndrome. Neuregulin 1, or NRG1, is a gene of the epidermal growth factor family and is involved in pathogenesis of schizophrenia.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman presents with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding, easy bruising, and prolonged bleeding after dental procedures. Her family history is significant for similar bleeding issues in her mother. Laboratory studies show a normal platelet count, prolonged aPTT as well as prolonged bleeding time. Platelet aggregation testing shows abnormal aggregation in the presence of ristocetin, but normal aggregation with ADP and collagen. Which of the following is NOT the most appropriate statement for her condition?

options.label: A
options.text: The affected factor helps in increasing serum half life of factor VIII

options.label: B
options.text: Acquired form may be associated with aortic valvular defect

options.label: C
options.text: Mild bleeding is associated with type III subtype

options.label: D
options.text: Autosomal dominant variant has mild bleeding

questions.answerText: Mild bleeding is associated with type III subtype
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Mild bleeding is associated with type III subtype 

 

  • Carrier of factor 8; and its increased serum half life (2.4 hours without it and 12 hours with it)
  • Acquired form of VWD – with Lymphoproliferative disorder or Heyde syndrome (Aortic stenosis + GI bleeding)
  • Autosomal dominant variant (type 1) has mild bleeding whereas type 3 has severe bleeding.
  • Type III vWD is the most severe form.
  • Very low or absent vWF
  • Severe bleeding, often resembling Hemophilia A
  • Profoundly low factor VIII levels
  • Key Features:
    • Young woman with mucocutaneous bleeding: Heavy menstruation, bruising, dental bleeding
    • Family history: Mother also affected → inherited
  • Laboratory findings:
    • Normal platelet count 
    • Prolonged aPTT (due to reduced factor VIII)
    • Prolonged bleeding time (due to defective platelet adhesion)
    • Ristocetin test abnormal (vWF-dependent platelet aggregation defect)
    • Normal aggregation with ADP and collagen (rules out platelet function disorders)
  • These findings are classic for vWD.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. The affected factor helps in increasing serum half-life of factor VIII: True.

 

  • vWF acts as a carrier protein for Factor VIII, protecting it from degradation.
  • Without vWF, Factor VIII levels drop → hence, aPTT is prolonged.
  • This is a correct statement.

 

Option B. Acquired form may be associated with aortic valvular defect: True

 

  • Acquired vWD can be seen in aortic stenosis (aka Heyde’s syndrome).
  • Shear stress across the stenotic valve causes proteolysis of vWF multimers.

 

Option D. Autosomal dominant variant has mild bleeding: True

 

  • Type I vWD is autosomal dominant, and the most common.
  • Partial quantitative deficiency of vWF
  • Bleeding is usually mild to moderate

questions.stemHtml: Match the following cancers with the respective genes involved:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) 1-D, 2-C, 3-A, 4-B

 

1. SDHB → Paraganglioma (D)

 

  • SDHB (Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Subunit B) is a tumor suppressor gene involved in the mitochondrial respiratory chain and Krebs cycle.
  • Mutations in SDHB are linked with hereditary paragangliomas and pheochromocytomas (tumors of extra-adrenal and adrenal chromaffin tissue).
  • Important point: SDHB mutations are associated with extra-adrenal paragangliomas and have a higher risk of malignancy.

 

2. K-RAS → Pancreatic carcinoma (C):

 

  • K-RAS (Kirsten Rat Sarcoma viral oncogene) is an oncogene coding for a GTPase involved in signal transduction.
  • Mutations in K-RAS lead to constitutive activation of downstream pathways (MAPK, PI3K) promoting uncontrolled cell growth.
  • It is one of the earliest and most frequent mutations in pancreatic adenocarcinoma, seen in ~90% of cases.
  • Also mutated in:
    • Colorectal carcinoma
    • Non-small cell lung cancer (especially adenocarcinoma subtype)

 

3. JAK2 → Myeloproliferative neoplasm (A):

 

  • JAK2 (Janus Kinase 2) is a cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase that transduces signals from cytokine receptors to the nucleus.
  • The V617F mutation in the JAK2 gene causes constitutive tyrosine kinase activity, leading to uncontrolled proliferation of hematopoietic cells.
  • This mutation is classically associated with Philadelphia-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms, including:
    • Polycythemia vera (PV) – ~95% of cases
    • Essential thrombocythemia (ET)
    • Primary myelofibrosis (PMF)

 

4. ALK → Adenocarcinoma lung (B):

 

  • ALK (Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase) gene rearrangements, especially EML4-ALK fusion, are involved in:
    • Lung adenocarcinoma – mostly seen in non-smokers, younger patients.
    • Also seen in anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor.
    • In lung cancer, ALK rearrangement leads to constitutive tyrosine kinase activity → cell growth and survival.
  • Targeted therapy available: Crizotinib, Ceritinib, Alectinib (ALK inhibitors).

questions.stemHtml: Match the following polyps with their respective genes involved:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) 1-D, 2-C, 3-A, 4-B

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a true statement about the most common leukemia in adults in the western world?

options.label: A
options.text: B cell cancer with origin from naïve B cell

options.label: B
options.text: Monoclonal lymphocytosis is a BCL2 overexpression due to deletion of chromosome 13q

options.label: C
options.text: Gumprecht cells are commonly seen on peripheral smear

options.label: D
options.text: Deletion of 17p is associated with good prognosis

questions.answerText: Deletion of 17p is associated with good prognosis
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Deletion of 17p is associated with good prognosis

 

Gumprecht cells or smudge cells represent mechanically damaged cells

 

Deletion of chromosome 13q leads to the loss of genes encoding microRNAs that are negative regulators of BCL2. 

 

Deletion of 17p is associated with poor prognosis

questions.stem: Which of the following kidney disorders is associated with a mutation in the COL4A3 chain?

options.label: A
options.text: A 45-year-old male presents with hematuria, proteinuria, and hearing loss

options.label: B
options.text: A 30-year-old female complains of shortness of breath and cough, and chest X-ray reveals pulmonary hemorrhage

options.label: C
options.text: A 25-year-old female undergoes renal biopsy showing thinning of glomerular basement membrane

options.label: D
options.text: A 50-year-old male presents with nephrotic syndrome and renal biopsy reveals nodular lesions in glomeruli.

questions.answerText: A 30-year-old female complains of shortness of breath and cough, and chest X-ray reveals pulmonary hemorrhage
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) A 30-year-old female complains of shortness of breath and cough, and chest X-ray reveals pulmonary hemorrhage

 

  • Suggestive of Goodpasture syndrome (anti-GBM disease)
  • Involves autoantibodies against the α3 chain of type IV collagen, not mutations in COL4A3.
  • It’s an autoimmune condition, not genetic.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A.  A 45-year-old male presents with hematuria, proteinuria, and hearing loss

COL4A3 Mutation – Alport Syndrome

  • The COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 genes encode type IV collagen, a critical structural component of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM).
  • Mutations in COL4A3 (and COL4A4) are commonly associated with:
    • Autosomal recessive Alport syndrome
    • Thin basement membrane disease (in milder forms)
    • Alport Syndrome Clinical Triad:
    • Hematuria (microscopic or gross)
    • Progressive proteinuria and renal dysfunction
    • Sensorineural hearing loss
    • ± Ocular defects (e.g., anterior lenticonus)

 

Option C. A 25-year-old female undergoes renal biopsy showing thinning of glomerular basement membrane: A 25-year-old female with GBM thinning on biopsy

 

  • Suggests Thin Basement Membrane Nephropathy (TBMN).
  • TBMN can be due to COL4A3/4 mutations, but it is often asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic.
  • While this could technically be correct, choice A better fits the classic full spectrum of COL4A3 mutation disease (Alport syndrome with hearing loss).

 

Option D. A 50-year-old male presents with nephrotic syndrome and renal biopsy reveals nodular lesions in glomeruli: A 50-year-old male with nephrotic syndrome and nodular glomerular lesions

 

  • Suggestive of Diabetic nephropathy or light chain deposition disease.
  • Not associated with COL4A3 mutations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not correctly matched?

options.label: A
options.text: IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation: skin rash after wasp bite

options.label: B
options.text: Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity: penicillin induced hemolytic anemia

options.label: C
options.text: Immune complex deposition: thrombocytopenia in SLE patients

options.label: D
options.text: T-cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity: Contact dermatitis due to poison ivy

questions.answerText: Immune complex deposition: thrombocytopenia in SLE patients
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Immune complex deposition: thrombocytopenia in SLE patients   

 

  • Immune complex deposition is Type III hypersensitivity, and it causes glomerulonephritis, vasculitis, arthritis, etc.
  • Thrombocytopenia in SLE is usually due to:
  • Autoantibody-mediated destruction of platelets → Type II hypersensitivity, not Type III.
  • IgG antibodies opsonize platelets → cleared by splenic macrophages.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation: skin rash after wasp bite: Correct match.

 

  • This is a Type I hypersensitivity reaction.
  • IgE binds to mast cells → allergen cross-links IgE → mast cell degranulation → histamine release → rash, urticaria, anaphylaxis.

 

Option B. Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC): penicillin-induced hemolytic anemia: Correct match.

 

  • This is a Type II hypersensitivity reaction.
  • Penicillin binds to RBCs → antibodies form against the drug-RBC complex → destruction via Fc receptor-mediated ADCC by NK cells or macrophages.

 

Option D. T-cell-mediated delayed hypersensitivity: Contact dermatitis due to poison ivy: Correct match.

 

  • Classic Type IV hypersensitivity.
  • T-cell response to hapten-protein complexes in skin → macrophage activation → dermatitis after 48–72 hours.

questions.stem: A patient is hospitalized for evaluation of a medical condition. A liver biopsy is taken and light microscopy shows extensive lymphocyte infiltration and granulomatous destruction of interlobular bile ducts. The biopsy was most likely taken from which of the following patients?

options.label: A
options.text: A 30-year-old homeless man with fever, abdominal pain, and jaundice

options.label: B
options.text: A 35-year-old man with a long history of ulcerative colitis who has fatigue and an elevated alkaline phosphatase

options.label: C
options.text: A 50-year-old obese woman with fever and a prolonged episode of severe right upper abdominal pain after fatty meal ingestion

options.label: D
options.text: A 50-year-old woman, with a long history of pruritus and fatigue who has pale stools and xanthelasma

questions.answerText: A 50-year-old woman, with a long history of pruritus and fatigue who has pale stools and xanthelasma
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) A 50-year-old woman, with a long history of pruritus and fatigue who has pale stools and xanthelasma

 

PBC is a chronic autoimmune liver disease characterized by destruction of intrahepatic, interlobular bile ducts by granulomatous inflammation. The disease typically presents insidiously with pruritus and fatigue in middle-aged women. Patients may eventually develop signs of cholestasis and hypercholesterolemia (eg, xanthelasma). 

 

Option A..viral hepatitis…..option B..PSC….option C…Cholecystitis

questions.stem: A 45-year-old male treated for sinusitis with ampicillin later develops fever. maculopapular skin rash, and oliguria. His serum creatinine level is 2.5 mg/dL. Urine sediment microscopy reveals red blood cells, neutrophils and eosinophils. The pathologic process in this patient's kidney most likely involves which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Renal interstitium

 

Fever, maculopapular rash and symptoms of acute renal failure one to three weeks after beginning treatment with a β-lactam antibiotic or a number of other drugs are highly suggestive of acute interstitial nephritis.  Peripheral eosinophilia and eosinophiluria are important clinical clues. Symptoms resolve completely after cessation of the medication.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is diagnosed with ALL after presenting with fever, pallor, and easy bruising. Laboratory studies show a white blood cell count of 22,000/mm³, hemoglobin of 7.5 g/dL, and platelet count of 60,000/mm³. Flow cytometry reveals that the blasts are positive for CD10 and CD19. Which of the following is the most favorable prognostic factor in this patient’s case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Hyperdiploidy (> 50 chromosomes)

 

Diagnosis of ALL is made. Favorable prognostic factors include age between 1 and 10 years, low initial WBC count (< 50,000/mm³), presence of hyperdiploidy, and certain immunophenotypes (e.g., CD10 positivity)

questions.stem: An elderly patient with history of smoking had a mass in the chest radiograph. The IHC of the pulmonary mass was positive for INSM 1. Which of the following is the most likely histological prerecursor lesion in this condition?

options.label: D
options.text: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia.

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) No known pre-invasive phase 

 

No known pre-invasive phase for small cell cancer of the lung. 

 

DIPNEH is an extremely rare but underdiagnosed pulmonary disorder at the benign end of the neuroendocrine cell proliferation spectrum of preinvasive lesions of the lungs

 

Intranuclear staining with INSM 1 for neuroendocrine origin tumors.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with increasing lower extremity edema over the past several weeks. Urinalysis shows 4+ proteinuria, no hematuria, and oval fat bodies. A renal biopsy has "spike and dome" appearance with special staining. Which of the following is the most unlikely finding of this patient's condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Subepithelial deposits seen on electron microscopy

options.label: B
options.text: Subendothelial deposits seen on electron microscopy

options.label: C
options.text: Presence of M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) as the antigen

options.label: D
options.text: IgG4 is the principal immunoglobulin deposited in most cases

questions.answerText: Subendothelial deposits seen on electron microscopy
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans B) Subendothelial deposits seen on electron microscopy

 

IgG4 (differs from other IgG subclasses as it a poor activator of the classical complement pathway, is the principal immunoglobulin deposited in most cases of membranous nephropathy

questions.stem: A known patient of Burkitt lymphoma undergoes chemotherapy following which he develops tumor lysis syndrome. All of the following may be seen with tumor lysis syndrome except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Hypercalcemia

 

  • Tumor lysis syndrome is associated with Burkitt lymphoma, acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), chronic tumors (CLL) and uncommonly solid tumors.
  • It is associated with hypocalcemia and not hypercalcemia.

questions.stemHtml: Match the following microscopic finding with the type of tumor:
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) 1-c, 2-d, 3-a, 4-b

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man presents to his primary care physician for an annual checkup. He has no significant complaints but mentions feeling "slower" in recent years. His physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory findings are within normal limits. Histologic examination of his liver biopsy, taken due to a mildly elevated liver enzyme noted in prior testing, shows granular, yellow-brown pigment within hepatocytes. This pigment does not stain with Prussian blue. Which of the following best describes this pigment?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Lipofuscin

 

Key Points:

 

  • Hemosiderin deposits stain positively with Prussian blue, distinguishing it from lipofuscin.
  • Lipofuscin is a "wear-and-tear" pigment that accumulates in cells over time, particularly in elderly individuals. It appears as a yellow-brown, granular cytoplasmic pigment, not reactive to Prussian blue, differentiating it from iron-containing pigments like hemosiderin.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman presents with a three-week history of new-onset headache, jaw pain while chewing, and blurry vision in her right eye. She also reports feeling fatigued and has a low-grade fever. Physical examination reveals scalp tenderness over the right temple. which of the following is not true about this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: High risk of loss of vision of the patient

options.label: B
options.text: Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells on histology

options.label: D
options.text: Internal elastic lamina fragmentation with VVG stain

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) High risk of renovascular hypertension

 

  • Renovascular hypertension is associated with fibromuscular dysplasia (young women) or atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis, not GCA.
  • GCA primarily affects the branches of the external and internal carotid arteries, not the renal arteries.

 

This 72-year-old woman has:

 

  • New-onset headache
  • Jaw claudication (pain while chewing)
  • Blurry vision (visual disturbance)
  • Scalp tenderness
  • Fever and fatigue

 

These are classic features of Giant Cell Arteritis (GCA), also known as temporal arteritis, a large-vessel vasculitis that affects elderly patients, especially women.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. High risk of loss of vision of the patient: True.

 

  • GCA commonly affects the ophthalmic artery, a branch of the internal carotid.
  • Leads to ischemic optic neuropathy → permanent vision loss.
  • Vision loss can be sudden and irreversible if not treated early with steroids.

 

Option B. Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells on histology: True.

 

  • Biopsy of the temporal artery reveals:
  • Granulomatous inflammation
  • Multinucleated giant cells
  • Intimal thickening
  • Fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina

 

 

Option D. Internal elastic lamina fragmentation with VVG stain: True.

 

  • Verhoeff-Van Gieson (VVG) stain highlights the internal elastic lamina, which shows fragmentation in GCA.
  • It's a diagnostic feature in temporal artery biopsy.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with neck pain, fever, and fatigue that began two weeks ago. She reports a recent upper respiratory infection. On examination, her thyroid gland is tender to palpation. Laboratory findings reveal an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

His mother reports that he recently had an upper respiratory infection. On examination, there is a palpable purpuric rash on his lower extremities and mild swelling of his knees and ankles. Urinalysis shows hematuria and mild proteinuria. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of his symptoms?

options.label: A

Physical examination reveals mucocutaneous candidiasis and hypoparathyroidism. Laboratory tests reveal hypocalcemia. Genetic testing shows a mutation in the AIRE gene. Which of the following mechanisms is primarily impaired in this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages

options.label: C

options.label: D

options.label: A
options.text: Oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria is impaired in cancer cells

options.label: B
options.text: Tumor cells preferentially use glycolysis to produce lactate for rapid energy production

options.label: C
options.text: Cancer cells have decreased numbers of mitochondria, necessitating glycolysis

options.label: D
options.text: Increased glucose uptake in cancer cells results from impaired insulin signaling

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Tumor cells preferentially use glycolysis to produce lactate for rapid energy production



erentially use glycolysis to produce lactate for rapid energy production

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman presents to the clinic with symptoms of fatigue, joint pain, and a facial rash that worsens with sun exposure. Laboratory tests reveal the presence of anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA) and low complement levels. Which of the following mechanisms is primarily responsible for the contributing to her pathogenesis?

options.label: C
options.text: Failure of B cell receptor editing

questions.answerText: Failure of B cell receptor editing
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Failure of B cell receptor editing 

 

Central tolerance is the mechanism by which self-reactive T and B cells are eliminated during their development in the thymus and bone marrow, respectively. This process ensures that lymphocytes with receptors strongly recognizing self-antigens are either deleted or undergo receptor editing before they can mature and enter the peripheral circulation. This mechanism is crucial in preventing autoimmunity. In SLE, a breakdown in tolerance mechanisms can lead to the survival of self-reactive lymphocytes, contributing to the development of autoimmunity.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Antigen presentation by dendritic cells is important for initiating immune responses, but it does not directly prevent autoimmunity through tolerance mechanisms.

 

Option B. Somatic hypermutation occurs in B cells to increase antibody affinity, not related to preventing autoimmunity.

 

Option D. Clonal deletion is required for reducing the chances of auto-immune disorders. 

 

Thus, central tolerance is the primary mechanism that prevents autoimmunity by eliminating self-reactive lymphocytes during their development.

questions.stem: Which of the following cannot be the presenting feature of Hodgkin lymphoma? Rapid growing mass affecting Waldeyer’s ringPainless cervical lymphadenopathy GI polyps Rapid growing mass affecting mandible
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) 1, 3 and 4

questions.stem: Which of the following is most appropriate component for reducing the risk of graft verus host disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Irradiation

 

Done for preventing GVHD by inactivating T-lymphocytes, not to prevent febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions.

 

Other Options

 

Option A. Washed RBCs: Washing RBCs can remove plasma proteins and antibodies, which might help in preventing allergic reactions, but it is not the primary method to prevent febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions caused by WBCs.

 

Option B. Leuko-reduced red blood cells: (RBCs) can help reduce the rate of transfusion reactions (especially febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions) in patients receiving recurrent transfusions. 

 

Option C. Immunosuppressive therapy: it is given to reduce the risk of graft rejection and not for reducing the GVHD.

questions.stem: All of the following statements about proto-oncogenes are true except? BRCA2 is an oncogene.HER2/Neu is amplified only in a fraction of breast cancer.EGFR (+) is seen in non-small cell lung cancer.C-MYC is a tumour suppressor gene.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) 1, 4

 

1 and 4 are false statements as BRCA2 is a tumor suppressor gene and C-MYC is a proto-oncogene.

questions.stemHtml: During a football match, where a young 20-year-old athlete tragically collapsed and was subsequently rushed to the hospital. Despite all efforts, the medical team could not save him, and he was pronounced deceased. The autopsy image provided gives us important information to investigate the cause of his untimely passing. What can be the most unlikely association of his condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Defect in beta myosin heavy chain

options.label: C
options.text: Sudden cardiac death due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

options.label: D
options.text: Sudden cardiac death due to arrhythmia

questions.answerText: Sudden cardiac death due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Sudden cardiac death due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

 

  • Gross Image (Left): Shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy with narrowed left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which is characteristic of HCM.
  • Microscopic Image (Right): Shows myofiber disarray, a hallmark histological feature of HCM.
  • HCM is one of the leading causes of SCD in young athletes.
  • Especially during strenuous activity.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Defect in beta myosin heavy chain:

 

  • Likely association
  • One of the most common genetic mutations in familial HCM (especially MYH7 gene).
  • Strongly linked with the pathogenesis.

 

Option B. Dynamic outflow obstruction:

 

  • Likely association
  • Seen in HCM due to systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve and septal hypertrophy.
  • Can cause exertional symptoms and syncope.

 

Option D. Sudden cardiac death due to arrhythmia

 

  • Most UNLIKELY in this specific context, although still possible
  • While arrhythmia is a mechanism of death in HCM, this option is nonspecific and can occur in many cardiac conditions (e.g., channelopathies, myocarditis).
  • It is less directly associated with the pathological features shown, unlike the other options that specifically point to HCM.

questions.stem: In which of the following phenomenon, “cell in cell” appearance is seen associated with degradation of the engulfed cell?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Entosis

options.label: A
options.text: Antigens recognized are lipid antigens without MHC proteins

options.label: B
options.text: Antigens recognized are protein antigens without MHC proteins

options.label: D
options.text: CD3 is required for antigen recognition

questions.answerText: Antigens recognized are lipid antigens without MHC proteins
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Antigens recognized are lipid antigens without MHC proteins

 

Gamma-delta (γδ) T cells can recognize Lipids WITHOUT MHC proteins. They are especially vital against mycobacterial infections. These receptors do not require MHC molecules for activation.

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Basal Cell Carcinoma

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Membranous glomerulopathy

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a rapidly enlarging mass in her left breast. She reports no pain but notes that the mass has grown significantly over the past few months. Physical examination reveals a firm, mobile breast mass measuring 6 cm. A core needle biopsy reveals stromal overgrowth with leaf-like projections. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Phyllodes tumor

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman presents with vague abdominal pain and weight loss. Physical examination reveals hepatomegaly. Laboratory tests show normal levels of alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and no evidence of hepatitis infection. Imaging studies reveal a large liver mass with a central scar. A biopsy is performed, and histology shows tumor cells with a distinctive fibrous lamellar pattern. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma 

 

HCC variant occurring in young adults without underlying liver disease or elevated AFP. It typically presents as a large mass with a central scar and distinctive lamellar fibrosis on histology.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Hepatic adenoma: Benign tumor, often associated with OCP/anabolic steroids; do not typically present with a fibrous lamellar pattern, nor do they usually have a central scar as seen in fibrolamellar HCC.

 

Option B. Focal nodular hyperplasia: Presents as a liver lesion with a central scar, but it is a benign lesion composed of normal hepatocytes and lacks the fibrous lamellar pattern seen in fibrolamellar HCC. 

 

Option D. Conventional HCC: Often has elevated AFP; lacks the distinctive lamellar fibrosis and is rarely seen in young adults without liver disease.
